terminus.finding: A network-metropolitan research document treats connection and disconnection as simultaneous: villages, firms, universities, corridors and e-commerce sites can become distributed nodes while monopoly, exclusion, information control and political cut-off remain possible.
terminus.generated: TOPOLOGY / POWER SPLIT MODEL: distributing local interfaces can lower access costs without destroying habitat, but distributed nodes do not automatically mean distributed control. A system may be spatially or topologically distributed while standards, data, capital, switching authority or exclusion power remain centralized. The prior DISTRIBUTED-SUPPORT-NODE model therefore needs two separate tests: interface distribution and control distribution.
terminus.relationToPrevious: Refines DISTRIBUTED-SUPPORT-NODE by adding a control layer and preventing a romantic equation of distribution with decentralization.
